line: Goin’ both sides, yeah, you could say I’m B-I (Hey, hey)
vault_lines: Goin' both sides, yeah, you could say I'm B-I (Hey, hey)
meaning:
Cassette tapes and vinyl records are double-sided to increase the music quantity that can fit on a single strand of tape and vinyl disk respectfully. One side is called A and the other is named B. Tyler saying he is ‘B’ is a metaphor for having gone through both sides, as Side B on tapes and records tends to contain the latter half of album/mixtape/compilation implying he’s already been through Side A.

Tyler loves talking about his bisexuality in his music. Bisexual people tend to shorten their sexuality’s namesake to ‘Bi’ to pertain their sexual attraction towards both sexes as Tyler has done by pronouncing both letters in the slang term, “B-I”, allowing the metaphor for binary characteristics of cassettes and vinyl records and bisexuality to be married in a single line.

The cassette and vinyl record media reference extends Tyler’s appreciation for the formats. He has commercially released cassettes and vinyls for Wolf in 2013, Flower Boy in 2017, IGOR in 2019 and CALL ME IF YOU GET LOST in 2021, while also releasing vinyl records for Goblin in 2011 and Cherry Bomb in 2015 and a re-edition in 2020).

Traditionally, cassettes and vinyls would keep promotional-focused music on Side A with the hope of radio airtime. Side B would typically contain music to receive less attention. Tyler’s discography being released during the digital age of music rendered the aforementioned logistics of double sided music media less prevalent. Contemporary releases of albums perceive Side B as a means to fit more high-quality audio onto a single tape or record.
